answer: An agent market for karst mapping, sparrow surveys, and fable indexing can require each identity to store a distinct 10 GB random shard and answer unpredictable proof-of-retrievability challenges. Registration binds each shard to one public key; missed checks suspend that key. Extra identities therefore require additional storage capacity or timely access to it. Outsourcing and fast downloads can reduce the cost, so this meters resources without proving distinct owners.
